status: WRITTEN preliminary all-variable exact T2 reduction, conditional on the UNREVIEWED 2+2 theorem and adopted f215; one consolidated proof packet in preparation
split: Independently Schur-triangularize arbitrary original traceless A,B and split each into 2+2 block-diagonal tracezero part and strictly upper 2×2 offblock. Let Q∈C^(16×2) have Q†Q=I. D_Q maps the 14-complex-dimensional diagonal coefficient space to (A_d⊗I+I⊗B_d)Q; N_Q maps the 8-complex-dimensional offblock coefficient space to (E↑⊗I+I⊗F↑)Q. Set D=2I−D_Q†D_Q, N=2I−N_Q†N_Q, J=D_Q†N_Q. Candidate 2+2 theorem gives D⪰0; f215 square-normal case gives N⪰0 because E↑²=F↑²=0.
exact_residual: For all original A,B, unrestricted T2 is equivalent to, for every Q, (i) ker D⊆ker J† and (ii) N−J†D^+J⪰0, by the singular Schur complement. Here D is 14×14, N is 8×8, D^+ is Moore-Penrose; no invertibility is assumed. The remaining 8×8 residual is exactly the block-coupling gap, not an automatic consequence of D,N⪰0.
sharper_first_unpaid_premise: ker D⊆ker J† is equivalent to: for each saturated block-diagonal pair X_d with D_Q(a_d)=saturation and P=QQ†, both upper-right 2×2 blocks Π1 Tr_B(X_d P) Π2 and Π1 Tr_A(X_d P) Π2 vanish. If P commutes with all four 2+2 sector projectors they do vanish. In particular, for any nonzero saturated X_d with σ2(X_d)>σ3(X_d), the maximizing P is the unique top-two spectral projector and is sector block-diagonal; only cutoff-degenerate σ2=σ3 points need the kernel condition checked. The 8×8 Schur inequality remains independently unpaid.
